summary: Unexpected routing to batch-optimized fallback causing abrupt p99 spikes and timeout errors
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ZenoRetail, dedicated) is seeing sudden p99 latency spikes and a wave of 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-10 ~09:15 UTC. Traffic that normally hits the low-latency variant is being routed to a batch-optimized fallback variant which has significantly longer cold-start and per-request latency under typical single-request traffic patterns. Impact: several production storefront features were rate-limited by the customer, affecting order recommendations and search autocomplete.

Impact:
- Observed p50/p95/p99 jump by ~2x/3x/6x respectively during incidents.
- ~1.2% of requests returned 504 over a 30-minute window; customer reports user-facing timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (ZenoRetail, reserved GPUs) in us-west-1
- Models involved: gptx-8k-lowlatency-v2 (preferred) and gptx-8k-batch-opt-quantized (fallback)

Notes: This ticket captures the investigation into why routing picked a slower batch-optimized fallback variant and why that variant experienced cold starts and head-of-line latency effects when receiving diverted traffic.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send steady single-request traffic to customer route (ZenoRetail prod) with typical query size (avg 450 tokens).
2) Simulate a capacity fluctuation by marking 2/6 low-latency replicas as unhealthy (or drain them).
3) Observe routing decisions in console and send synthetic load at 10r/s.
4) Measure p99 and number of 504 responses.
Expected: traffic should go to warm, low-latency replicas or queued smartly; NotExpected: immediate diversion to batch-optimized variant leading to cold starts and higher p99.
observed_behavior: Routing component diverted a large share of incoming requests to the batch-optimized variant (gptx-8k-batch-opt-quantized). That variant has batching enabled and fewer warm replicas; when it received single-shot traffic it started serial long-running warmups (coldstarts) and large request batching which caused head-of-line delays and subsequent 504s when upstream timeouts hit.
expected_behavior: When preferred low-latency replicas are unavailable, routing should prefer warm, low-latency alternatives, or apply gradual spillover with pre-warm steps. Fallback to batch-optimized variants should be a last resort and should not receive latency-sensitive single-request traffic until warmed.

investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 09:15 UTC: first spike; router logs show policy 'cost_saver' triggered fallback to batch variant when healthcheck transient failed for 2 replicas.
- 09:16-09:20 UTC: batch variant began initializing replicas; warm cache/KV not present -> coldstarts. Batching logic combined single requests into larger batches causing head-of-line delays.
- 09:25 UTC: autoscaler observed low sustained concurrency on the batch variant and did not spawn enough warm replicas; policy has a minimum_warm_replicas config but it was mis-set for dedicated pools created by onboarding script v1.4.
Hypothesis:
- Newer routing policy introduced in routing PR #212 favors cost-optimized fallback earlier in the failover sequence under the name 'cost_saver'. The policy does not respect the 'avoid_batch_on_single_request' flag for dedicated pools.
- Onboarding script set minimum_warm_replicas=0 for batch variants leading to no pre-warmed replicas in this pool.
Verification steps run:
- Replayed traffic in staging with two replicas artificially marked unhealthy: reproduced p99 spikes when fallback policy allowed batch variant to accept single-shot requests.
- Confirmed config discrepancy between dedicated pool templates (min_warm=0) and hosted defaults (min_warm=2).
workaround: Applied temporary mitigation at 2026-03-10T10:05 UTC: routing override was applied to pin ZenoRetail to gptx-8k-lowlatency-v2 and disabled the 'cost_saver' fallback for this route. Added a warm replica to batch-optimized variant in case further spillover is needed. Customer confirmed reduction in 504s and p99 dropped back toward normal in ~10 minutes.
next_steps:
1) Roll back or patch routing policy 'cost_saver' to respect the 'avoid_batch_on_single_request' flag for dedicated pools (owner: routing team, PR #212 follow-up).
2) Update onboarding template so minimum_warm_replicas >= 2 for any variant that may be used for latency-sensitive routes (owner: infra/onboarding).
3) Add an e2e test that simulates replica drain and verifies fallback choices don't route single-shot traffic to batch-optimized variants.
4) Postmortem to be created and linked to this ticket; notify product about potential UI option to pin fallback behavior per-customer.
5) Schedule customer-facing summary and follow-up with ZenoRetail CS lead.
